transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Khatri (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Praxis Head of ML Ops), Liam O'Connor (Praxis CTO), Sara Patel (Praxis Cloud Engineer), Diego Ramirez (Praxis Product)

Summary:
Quick QBR / health check: usage trends, cost anomalies, reliability incidents, roadmap alignment for next quarter, and path to pilot Dedicated capacity. Agreed to run benchmark and share pricing options + SOC2/security artifacts.

Topics:
- Usage & cost (token volume, embedding vs llm calls)
- Reliability incidents (spike on 2026-02-28; timeout errors)
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, burst capacity
- Security / compliance (SOC 2, SAML SSO, KMS/HSM, audit logs)
- Roadmap: model upgrades, quantization, batching improvements

Action items (captured): see metadata list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Moreno: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, this is our QBR for Praxis, we'll do a quick health check then go into roadmap and next steps.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Thanks Alex, yeah big week, trying to get alignment before our next infra review.
[00:31] Priya Khatri: Quick note — I'll start with usage and cost trends then hand over to Alex for pricing, ok?
[00:42] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. we had a big uptick in inference in late February when the recommender roll out happened, so curious about how caching and batching is behaving.
[00:57] Priya Khatri: Right, we see the ramp — your token volume jumped ~3.2x for generation requests and embeddings are steady. The good news is prefix/KV cache hits are around 28% on average but on the long tail the cache misses cause CPU/GPU burst.
[01:17] Sara Patel: We noticed some increased p99 latency during the surge and a few timeouts, we filed a ticket, not sure if that was autoscaler config or a model slowdown.
[01:31] Priya Khatri: There was a cluster autoscale edge case — we throttle to maintain latency SLO and sometimes requests hit fallback which increases tail latency. We pushed a patch last week that helps scaling granularity.
[01:45] Maya Chen: Can you explain fallback? is that Redwood's fallback to smaller model or to hosted?
[01:52] Alex Moreno: Yeah fallback policy — we route to compatible model variants or to Hosted pool depending on your routing rules. For Praxis you currently have a mixed policy: prefer Dedicated but allow Hosted fallback during sustained capacity limits.
[02:12] Diego Ramirez: That is correct, we wanted continuity during peak but want to control cost.
[02:19] Priya Khatri: Cost note — dedicated baseline reduces per-token cost at high volume but introduces committed spend. We laid out a few profiles: reserved GPU slots with burst credits, or pure hosted with autoscaling. We'll attach the model to the sheet.
[02:36] Liam O'Connor: We care about predictable latency for user-facing recommender; can you share hard SLO numbers?
[02:44] Priya Khatri: For your current model and sequence lengths, we can target 95th percentile sub-200ms on dedicated pools with right batching; hosted averages are 250-350ms depending on load. We'll run a benchmark to confirm.
[03:02] Sara Patel: OK. Also procurement asked about encryption and audit logs — do you provide KMS integration, HSM, and detailed request logging?
[03:12] Alex Moreno: Yes — Redwood Private/Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations, and audit logs with token-level traces in the Console. We can share SOC 2 artifacts and architecture docs.
[03:28] Maya Chen: Are the logs shipable to our CloudWatch? We want to centralize.
[03:34] Alex Moreno: Yes we support log forwarding to S3/CloudWatch via an integration; we'll include the example IAM role.
[03:42] Liam O'Connor: On SSO, we need SAML with SCIM provisioning for users and RBAC controls.
[03:49] Jordan Lee: We have SAML and SCIM support, plus per-team RBAC in Console. We can demo provisioning flows in the next call.
[03:59] Diego Ramirez: Any compliance gaps? we need SOC 2 Type II and a few EU data residency notes.
[04:07] Alex Moreno: SOC 2 Type II is available, and we offered EU-region private deployments for data residency. We'll share the compliance pack — redact by default.
[04:18] Priya Khatri: Back to reliability, we saw the incident on 2026-02-28 — brief overview: a model rollout coincided with a surge and the canary didn't catch a memory leak on one variant, autoscaler oscillated, we had a few requeues. We fixed the model variant config and adjusted rolling policy.
[04:40] Maya Chen: That explains it. Any suggestion to avoid this in future?
[04:44] Priya Khatri: Recommend canary for 5-10% traffic with health probes, and slow ramp A/B with automated rollback on mem/latency regressions. Also consider pinned model versions for critical endpoints.
[04:58] Sara Patel: For the prod recommender we'd like pinned versions and a canary window. What's the rollback time?
[05:04] Priya Khatri: Rollback can be automatic within 1-3 minutes once health checks alert, depending on KV cache warm-up; warm-up may temporarily increase latency while cache rebuilds.
[05:16] Liam O'Connor: Wanted to surface one more cost spike — last month's bill had a single job that consumed lots of long-context tokens for debugging. Any guardrails?
[05:26] Alex Moreno: You can set per-route quotas and token limits. We also recommend separate API keys for debugging jobs and scheduled pruning of long-context logs.
[05:36] Maya Chen: Great. For roadmap — we're interested in quantization advice and model selection to reduce cost without losing quality.
[05:45] Priya Khatri: We can run a quantization evaluation and suggest 4-bit/8-bit profiles per model. Also Redwood Optimize will recommend kernel and batch settings per workload.
[05:57] Diego Ramirez: Do you support custom kernels for our proprietary model?
[06:01] Priya Khatri: We can onboard custom models — there's a model onboarding process; may require model conversion and compatibility checks, will likely need an SE-led scoping call.
[06:12] Sara Patel: We also need a performance baseline run with our test harness. How long does that take?
[06:18] Priya Khatri: Typical 1-hour end-to-end benchmark; we run varying sequence lengths and concurrency and produce a report. We'll ask you to provide the harness and we run it in a dedicated cluster.
[06:29] Alex Moreno: OK action: Priya will schedule the benchmark; Alex will send pricing options for Dedicated/reserved + burst.
[06:36] Liam O'Connor: Procurement timeline — we hope to decide by end of March, ideally start pilot in April.
[06:42] Jordan Lee: Noted, internal SLAs and procurement constraints?
[06:46] Liam O'Connor: 3-6 month pilot, procurement needs a quote and compliance pack.
[06:51] Maya Chen: On instrumentation, can Redwood provide token-level cost breakdowns per route?
[06:58] Alex Moreno: Yes that's in the Console — per-route token counts, cost breakdown by model and token type. We'll share screenshots.
[07:07] Sara Patel: Any tips to reduce cost with minimal quality loss?
[07:11] Priya Khatri: Mix of caching, prompt compression, and model quantization; also structured output and function calling can reduce token churn.
[07:21] Diego Ramirez: We were also exploring routing by policy — like route low-latency queries to dedicated and experimental ones to hosted. Is that possible?
[07:29] Priya Khatri: Yes routing policies are configurable; you can set latency-first or cost-first. We can show example config.
[07:36] Liam O'Connor: Are there any network requirements for Private deployment?
[07:40] Alex Moreno: For Private you need VPC peering or PrivateLink and a few firewall rules; we'll send the network guide.
[07:49] Maya Chen: For the benchmark, we want 95/99 p to be recorded and KV cache stats. Also please include warm and cold cache runs.
[07:58] Priya Khatri: Absolutely. We'll include cold/warm runs and KV hit/miss ratios in the report.
[08:05] Sara Patel: On observability, can we get traces into our APM?
[08:09] Jordan Lee: We have trace export integrations (Jaeger/OTLP) and can forward spans.
[08:15] Diego Ramirez: Any blockers for starting the pilot?
[08:19] Alex Moreno: Only procurement and network access; technical onboarding is quick. We need the test harness and access for benchmark.
[08:27] Liam O'Connor: Ok scheduling — can we aim for benchmark week of Mar 22 and decision by end of March?
[08:33] Alex Moreno: Yes that matches our timelines.
[08:38] Maya Chen: One more detail — we need to ensure data residency for EU users. We have a portion of user base in Ireland.
[08:46] Alex Moreno: We can pin workloads to EU regions or run Private in your region. We'll note that in proposal.
[08:54] Priya Khatri: Quick clarifier — when you said the 28% cache hit, is that across all endpoints?
[08:59] Sara Patel: That was aggregate; some endpoints have higher hits.
[09:03] Priya Khatri: We'll break that down by route in the benchmark.
[09:09] Jordan Lee: Also we'll include a recommended rollout plan for canarying and rollback playbook.
[09:15] Diego Ramirez: Great.
[09:17] Alex Moreno: Any blockers from the Praxis side?
[09:21] Maya Chen: Need to confirm that procurement team will accept SOC2 and our security review timeline.
[09:27] Liam O'Connor: We'll triage internally.
[09:31] Alex Moreno: Perfect. Recap of next steps: Alex sends pricing & proposal, Priya schedules and runs benchmark, Sara provides network/logs, Jordan uploads QBR notes and schedules procurement follow-up.
[09:49] Maya Chen: Thanks all.
[09:51] Alex Moreno: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with artifacts.
[10:00] End of recording.

Notes on transcription quality: there are occasional mis-hearings of product names (e.g., Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as 'Redwood Dedecated'), and technical acronyms may be spaced out (K V cache). The transcript is verbatim-ish with filler words and overlaps.
